title: LIKE/ILIKE/regex, CASE, string and date functions
summary: Compute in the database instead of in the app: case-insensitive matching with ILIKE, conditional labels with CASE, and formatted output with to_char.

examples.title: ILIKE, CASE labels and to_char formatting

annotations.note: ILIKE lowercases both sides with the database's case rules. StackLab's databases use the builtin C.UTF-8 locale, so Ş/ş and İ/i fold, but Turkish I/ı never pair up: 'ISPARTA' ILIKE 'ısparta' is false. Appending COLLATE "tr-x-icu" switches to Turkish rules.
A searched CASE without ELSE yields NULL when no branch matches, which is why Quiet day gets a NULL label.
Dy and Mon always print English abbreviations. The TM prefix (TMDy, TMMon) translates them using the server's lc_time setting instead.

use_cases: Search boxes: ILIKE '%term%' over names and titles
Reports: CASE labels, to_char formatted dates, grouped totals
strengths: Shaping happens once, in the database, close to the data and its indexes
CASE works everywhere an expression does: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, aggregates
to_char formats dates in the query itself; with the TM prefix, month and day names follow the server's lc_time
weaknesses: Leading-wildcard ILIKE cannot use a btree index; large tables need pg_trgm or full-text search
ILIKE follows the database's case rules: under the default (non-Turkish) mapping, I and ı never match; Turkish rules need COLLATE "tr-x-icu"
Heavy string formatting in SQL moves presentation logic away from the app

pitfalls.title: CASE without ELSE returning NULL
pitfalls.detail: Rows matching no branch come back NULL, which then fails comparisons and concatenation downstream. Add an ELSE when 'other' means something.

pitfalls.title: Trusting to_char for machine-readable output
pitfalls.detail: to_char is presentation and depends on session settings; keep timestamps raw in the wire format and format in the client when the app must compute on them.

quiz.why: ILIKE is PostgreSQL's case-insensitive LIKE; standard SQL has no equivalent.

quiz.q: What does a CASE expression without ELSE return when no branch matches?
quiz.why: A missed CASE yields NULL, which then interacts with three-valued logic downstream.

body:
## Concept

Every row you ship to the app is a row the app must re-shape. Postgres can do
the shaping: `ILIKE` for case-insensitive search, `CASE` for conditional labels,
`to_char` for formatted dates, and the string functions (`upper`, `left`,
`split_part`) for light text munging. The result reads like a tiny report
written in SQL.

`CASE` comes in two forms — searched (`CASE WHEN cond THEN ...`) and simple
(`CASE x WHEN v THEN ...`) — and both return NULL when nothing matches and no
ELSE is given, which connects back to three-valued logic.

## Coming from C/C++/Java/Python/JS

If you reach for the application layer for formatting, this is the lesson that
moves that code. Python: think of `CASE` as a per-row conditional expression
(`x if cond else y`); `to_char` is `strftime` with Postgres's own format
specifiers — note they differ from strftime's codes. Java: `String.format`
lives in the database now, and the format survives whichever client queries
next. JavaScript: this is the work you'd otherwise do in a `.map()` after
fetching — doing it in SQL means less data over the wire and one less place
for the formatting to drift.

## Design notes

Postgres deliberately blurs "expression" and "report": CASE is an expression, so
it sorts, filters and aggregates like any other value; to_char exists so that a
report can come out of the database already formatted (with TM-prefixed patterns,
in the server's lc_time language). The split to keep in mind
is data versus rendering — keep the wire format raw (timestamptz, plain text)
and reach for these functions for evidence-shaped queries and human output, not
for storage formats.

files.examples/01_patterns.sql:
CREATE TABLE events (
  id        serial PRIMARY KEY,
  title     text NOT NULL,
  kind      text NOT NULL,
  starts_at timestamp NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO events (title, kind, starts_at) VALUES
  ('Deploy window', 'ops',    '2026-11-12 09:00:00'),
  ('Istanbul meetup', 'talk', '2026-11-12 18:30:00'),
  ('istanbul study group', 'talk', '2026-11-13 19:00:00'),
  ('Quiet day', 'other', '2026-11-14 12:00:00');

-- Case-insensitive search: ILIKE lowercases both sides, then matches.
SELECT title FROM events WHERE title ILIKE '%istanbul%';

-- Conditional labels: searched CASE, NULL when nothing matches (no ELSE).
SELECT title,
       CASE WHEN kind = 'ops'  THEN 'maintenance'
            WHEN kind = 'talk' THEN 'community'
       END AS label
FROM events
ORDER BY id;

-- to_char renders timestamps the way reports want them.
SELECT title, to_char(starts_at, 'Dy DD Mon HH24:MI') AS when
FROM events
ORDER BY starts_at;
